criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Every frame is rendered in one world and two frames come close to the 10. Slide 1 is the best: the furrows are raked correctly by a west sun, with a barbed-wire fence, a near lath with its flag and contact, and flagged rows on the horizon band. Slide 9 has real atmosphere, with poles receding, the pickup and haze. The rest of the deck is held down by four things. (1) THE HOUR DOES NOT READ. The chassis declares goldenHour with the sun at elevation 7, but the sky on slides 1 to 8 is flat slate grey with no warm band and no sun, with visible banding steps, and on slide 9 the sun disc sits roughly 25 degrees up. (2) DEFAULTS AND ARTIFACTS ON SEVERAL FRAMES. Slide 7 is a sine-ripple water plane with a flat black strip and a drowned lath reading as a stick on a dark puck. Slide 5's hall is a frontal backdrop with broken louvre slats and no visible long shadows. Slide 2's pulled lath floats at the height of the fence wire. Slide 8's ground is featureless and its blocks are flat tan tiles. (3) TYPE ON PLATES. On slides 8 and 9 the kicker and counter each sit on a visible blurred dark patch. (4) DOSSIER ELEMENTS NEVER RENDERED. Slide 3 has no FM 112, no houses and no berm. Slide 6 has no cedar elms and the berm has nothing to give it a 6 foot scale. The 7 descriptor allows one frame to lean on a default and this deck has four or five.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: Clearly one deck: one prairie chassis, one hero (the 6 foot pine lath with survey-pink flagging) on all nine frames, the motif changing state on every frame. Slides 1 and 2 share a camera to the pixel. Slide 6's warm grassy hillside doesn't look like the black-clay field of 1 and 2, and slide 9's high sun breaks the one-light law.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces: 664 c2, 700/500/400 c31 c32, 6 c33 plus the labelled drawing rule, 65/85 c12 c13, 1.575 c17, about 1,400 c52, $28.2 million c35 with its parts summing. The petition outcome is KEYE's and the dek says so. Slide 1's dek 'Each flagged stake stands at a distance its terms set' is looser than its picture, since the near stake stands a few metres inside the fence. Slide 3 draws a hall at 700 feet without slide 5's 'drawn for scale'.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: Body, place, decision and deadline are named. The stake is drawn as feet and decibels, and the caption's closing question is a real open term. What a reader can do next is implied rather than stated.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover stops the scroll, slide 2 pays at once, the deck turns on slide 8 and the close lands on the date and the money. Slides 5 and 6 restate slide 3's distances.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register. Some lines read as procedure ('The slides stake each distance.', 'Each flagged stake stands at a distance its terms set.'). The world's regional specificity reaches the art more than the copy.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: A fresh concept. The accent is the same magenta family as no. 42's, and the dark register and wide establishing opening repeat no. 43 and no. 41.

one_sentence_fix: Make the declared goldenHour world appear on every frame with a warm low-sun band, move slide 9's sun down to elevation 7, and rebuild slide 7's basin with visible clay banks and a still reflective surface.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Sine-ripple water plane with no visible banks, a flat black strip across the frame, the drowned lath a stick on a dark puck.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the 2 to 1 clay banks with a damp band at the waterline, a near-still reflective surface, delete the black strip and sink the lath to its knot.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The hall is a frontal backdrop with broken louvre slats, the stakes cast no visible shadow, and the mid-ground is empty.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Turn the camera about 25 degrees so the hall's west end recedes and catches the low sun, and let each lath throw a long cast east.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The pulled lath floats at the height of the fence wire with its shadow detached.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop it onto a furrow ridge in the near lower right with a contact under its whole length, at least 400 px long and apart from the wire.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Featureless ground, flat tan tiles, and the kicker and counter on blurred dark patches.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Put worked-clay furrow ground under the blocks and remove the sky scrims by tilting the camera down.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The berm reads as a grassy hillside with no 6 foot scale, no elms, flat light.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Put the lath at the toe in the near third, add kit cedar elms, and swing the camera so the low sun rakes the crest.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The sun sits about 25 degrees up against the declared 7, the flagging is a flat unlit polygon, and the furniture sits on blurred patches.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the sun onto the horizon band, shade the flagging with a lit material, and remove the plates behind the furniture.
